title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing & padding minimization optimizations
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves dynamic batching by grouping requests into sequence-length buckets and minimizing per-batch padding; reduces avg token latency and increases throughput for skewed seqlen workloads. No API changes.
commits: a1b2c3: introduce seqlen bucketing data structures and bucket assignment logic
d4e5f6: implement packing algorithm to minimize padding within a bucket
a7b8c9: scheduler hooks to prefer same-bucket coalescing and small-penalty rebalancing
b0c1d2: KV-cache aware eviction heuristics to keep hot prefixes for common seqlen buckets
c3d4e5: add benchmarks, perf tests and docs; tune kernel selection thresholds
description:
Context: production workloads show high seqlen variance (short prompts + long contexts). Existing continuous-batching aggregated by arrival time resulted in excessive padding, hurting throughput and latency for both short and long requests. This PR implements sequence-length bucketing with packing heuristics to minimize padding while preserving latency SLOs and KV-cache effectiveness.

What this PR does: - Adds a lightweight seqlen-bucketing layer in the batching pipeline that assigns incoming requests into discrete buckets based on effective sequence length percentiles (configurable buckets: 8, 16, 32, 64, 128). - Within each bucket, we run a packing algorithm that fills batches up to a target token budget instead of naive request-count batching; this reduces worst-case padding per batch. - Scheduler integration: the bucketing scheduler prefers coalescing same-bucket requests for a short window (configurable hold_time_ms) and allows limited cross-bucket joins when latency budgets are near saturation. - KV-cache awareness: added quick heuristics so the KV-cache keeps entries for hot prefixes observed in dominant buckets; when eviction is necessary, we prefer evicting cold buckets to avoid cache churn. - Kernel selection hints: emit per-bucket statistics to allow the runtime to pick optimized kernels (e.g., attention tiling) for common bucket sizes. - Benchmarks and CI: added microbenchmarks and an end-to-end perf test that runs in the bench pipeline; metrics exported for per-bucket latency and padding ratio.

Motivation and tradeoffs: - Primary goal is padding minimization for throughput improvement without harming tail latency. - Bucketing adds minimal scheduling overhead (<200ns per request) and reduces average per-batch padding by ~42% in our internal runs for mixed seqlen traces. - There is a small risk of increased latency for rare seqlen extremes if strict bucket isolation is used; we mitigate that with controlled cross-bucket joins and latency-based fallback. - KV-cache heuristic keeps hit-rate stable across buckets for benchmarks we care about.

Benchmarks (internal): - Workload: mixed corpus (40% short <=16, 40% medium 17-64, 20% long >64) on p4d-like nodes. - Baseline (continuous-time batching): avg token latency 9.8ms, throughput 12.3k tok/s, pad ratio 0.31. - This PR: avg token latency 8.1ms (-17%), throughput 14.6k tok/s (+19%), pad ratio 0.18 (-42%). - Tail (p99) latency unchanged within measurement noise (+1.5%). Full bench results and scripts are included under benchmarks/seqlen_bucketing.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/batching: seqlen_bucket.* implements bucket assignment, bucket-level packing and invariants. - runtime/scheduler: bucketing_scheduler.rs wires bucketed coalescing into the existing scheduler with hold windows and rebalancing logic. - runtime/kv_cache: eviction policy tuned to prefer bucket-locality. - tests/bench: added end-to-end perf test and synthetic traces to reproduce padding improvements. - docs: new perf notes and recommended default bucket configs.

Review conversation highlights: - @Evan Liu requested measurable knobs for bucket sizes and hold_time_ms; added config with sane defaults and unit tests (comment resolved). - @María Gonzales asked for KV-cache impact analysis; I added microbench marks and a short section in docs that shows KV hit-rate stability. - @Connor Smith suggested exposing per-bucket metrics in the console; added promql targets and an observability note. - CI initially had a flaky benchmark in bench-pipeline (timeout on long-run); extended timeout and moved heavy bench to a separate bench job to keep PR CI fast.

CI: - Unit tests: pass - Integration perf tests: pass on bench pipeline after re-run - Lint/format: pass - Codegen: pass

Merge: - Merged via squash after approvals and green CI. Changelog: Added performance improvements for dynamic batching by sequence length; no user-facing API changes.

Notes/follow-ups: - We should run a Canary on dedicated clusters with production workloads to validate KV-cache behavior for multi-tenant scenarios (ENG-927 follow-up). - Consider auto-tuning bucket boundaries from real traffic histograms in a future change (ENG-912).
notes_for_release: Enable seqlen bucketing behind runtime flag `enable_seqlen_bucketing`. Default ON for hosted; can be toggled per-deployment. Monitor batching_padding_ratio and per-bucket p50/p99.
